question: What does one pass over every open item in twelve repos cost in GraphQL points?
pass: Within the budget of section 7.3 (section 6), as the Maintainer's working ruling on #13 (2026-10-19) sets the method and FR-35 accepts a stated estimate: the pass's read, shaped as sections 4.1 and 3.3 have it (the full facts of each open pull request, the two-depth listing of each open issue, P-32's question in the same read), is made by the reader App on the two repos it reaches, and its cost taken from rateLimit of the same response; the counts of open pull requests and issues in every repo of the org are read through the Maintainer's login; the cost per pull request and per issue is extrapolated to those counts and multiplied by the passes an hour. It passes if a pass whose pages are sized to the counts costs under W-4's 3,000 points an hour at the twelve passes an hour of the schedule, section 7.3's option 2, which option 4 is built as first; the fixture also records the passes an hour the budget allows, so that the peak the relay's nudges can drive (a tick every minute or two, P-20) is judged against it, and costs the read a hundred wide, the design's words, and the fallback of section 4.1. The figure is an estimate.

request.call: POST /graphql (gh api graphql), the open pull requests and issues of every repo of the org, with rateLimit

body.query: query($org:String!){organization(login:$org){repositories(first:50,orderBy:{field:NAME,direction:ASC}){totalCount nodes{nameWithOwner isPrivate isArchived pullRequests(states:OPEN){totalCount} issues(states:OPEN){totalCount}}}} rateLimit{cost remaining limit resetAt nodeCount}}

headers.x-oauth-scopes: admin:org, admin:org_hook, delete_repo, gist, read:packages, read:project, repo, workflow

request.call: POST /graphql (gh api graphql), every open item's list sizes across the org in one query, which GitHub refused at its node limit

body.query: query($org:String!){organization(login:$org){repositories(first:50,orderBy:{field:NAME,direction:ASC}){nodes{nameWithOwner pullRequests(states:OPEN,first:100){nodes{number files(first:1){totalCount} labels(first:1){totalCount} reviews(first:1){totalCount} reviewThreads(first:1){totalCount} timelineItems(first:1,itemTypes:[LABELED_EVENT,UNLABELED_EVENT,REVIEW_DISMISSED_EVENT,ADDED_TO_MERGE_QUEUE_EVENT,REMOVED_FROM_MERGE_QUEUE_EVENT,READY_FOR_REVIEW_EVENT,CONVERT_TO_DRAFT_EVENT]){totalCount} commits(last:1){nodes{commit{statusCheckRollup{contexts(first:1){totalCount}}}}} closingIssuesReferences(first:1){totalCount}}} issues(states:OPEN,first:100){nodes{number labels(first:1){totalCount} timelineItems(first:1,itemTypes:[LABELED_EVENT,UNLABELED_EVENT]){totalCount} closedByPullRequestsReferences(first:1,includeClosedPrs:false){totalCount}}}}}} rateLimit{cost nodeCount remaining}}

body.formula: cost = max(1, round((2 + max(P,1) x (8 + T) + 3 x I) / 100))
body.T: the page of review threads asked for each pull request

body.method: The Maintainer's working ruling on #13 (2026-10-19). GitHub charges a GraphQL read by the connections it may have to make, not by what it returns: each connection costs the product of its ancestors' page sizes (a page of 0 counted as 1), the sum is divided by 100 and rounded, 1 at least. The model is held to every read above with a rateLimit (model_checks). The pass's read costs, per repo, 2 + P x (8 + T) + 3 x I calls: P open pull requests, each with eight connections and T thread pages (one comment each, for the opening actor), I open issues with three each. The reader App measured it on the two repos it reaches; the counts of every repo of the org came through the Maintainer's login; the per-repo figures below are that model at those counts, an estimate (FR-35), to be measured exactly when the first Consumer is onboarded. The counts are those of 01:17Z; software-factory had 2 open pull requests then and 1 from 01:19Z, when one merged. A list past a hundred (an issue page past the first, or an item's files, reviews, threads, checks or timeline past a hundred) is one more read, one point each, counted under further_pages from the survey's totals; sized_to_counts_every_page is the pass over every open item whole.
